baselines.title: Machine-accelerated extraction of experimental superconducting parameters for physical insight and prediction across thousands of materials

dataset.notes: Sources include open-access arXiv preprints plus a digitized Roberts (1976) survey. Entries preserve experimental method and relevant pressure, sample form, field orientation or measurement temperature when available. The paper describes data and method but no direct downloadable machine-readable dataset URL was confirmed in this inventory.

validation.notes: The paper identifies isolated extraction errors, including transient photoinduced or theoretical values misread as equilibrium experimental measurements.

baselines.split_characterization: Five-fold cross-validation with every evaluated family represented in training, plus explicit leave-one-family-out experiments.
baselines.claim_ceiling: Published experimental-property extraction and model baseline; not independently replayed by this repository.

baselines.title: Developing a complete AI-accelerated workflow for superconductor discovery
baselines.label_definition: DFT-derived Eliashberg spectral function and Allen-Dynes Tc

dataset.data_archive_rights_metadata: CC-BY-4.0 reported by B2FIND catalogue; verify archive's own record terms before redistribution
dataset.notes: The BEE-NET Git snapshot documents database.json and model checkpoints as untracked/not included. The archive contains around 7,000 electron-phonon calculations; BEE-NET states 5,241 entries in its selected database. The public GitHub repository snapshot has no LICENSE file discoverable through the contents endpoint; code reuse needs author/rights review.

baselines.split_characterization: Documented 20% held-out test set. No leave-one-family-out result is reported in the pinned README snapshot. The README warns that train/validation indices are DataFrame row labels while the test file contains Alexandria IDs; using the CIF index column rather than DataFrame labels would contaminate the test.
baselines.downstream_workflow: The paper reports a multi-stage pipeline from more than 1.3 million candidates to 741 computationally stable candidates and experimental synthesis/confirmation of two new superconductors.
baselines.claim_ceiling: Calculated-label spectral-function prediction and candidate screening baseline. Its MAE must not be compared as if it were measured experimental Tc.

baselines.title: Large language models for superconductor discovery

dataset.record_count_discrepancy: The paper abstract reports 78,203 records; a methods description has been reported as 78,204. Resolve from immutable released row IDs before reproduction.
dataset.sources: APS and Elsevier literature plus domain handbooks, as described by the paper
dataset.rights: Dataset, code and checkpoint-specific terms have not yet been fully admitted by this repository; verify before copying, redistribution, or retraining.

tasks: inverse design conditioned on target Tc
published_findings.unreported_candidate_claim: GNoME screening produced candidates with predicted Tc > 10 K; predictions are unverified and are not discoveries.

baselines.claim_ceiling: Published LLM extraction/prediction/inverse-design baseline; the 28% novelty fraction is relative to the paper's training set and does not establish physical novelty or synthesizability.

baselines.title: Towards the discovery of high critical magnetic field superconductors
baselines.source_version: npj Computational Materials accepted article (published 2026-08-12); arXiv:2601.21044

dataset.method: alpha2F(omega) spectral functions and DFT Fermi surfaces combined with clean-limit Eliashberg theory; strong-coupling and electron-phonon mass-renormalization effects included
dataset.notes: The article reports a consistent computational database covering approximately 7,300 superconductors. The accessible abstract identifies a Supplementary Information file, but this inventory has not yet verified a public machine-readable bulk data archive, immutable artifact digest, or code snapshot. Exact row count and conditions must be pinned before reproduction.

qualitative: unexpectedly large number of Type-I superconductors
larger unit cells generically support higher critical fields and Type-II behaviour
strong-coupling and electron-phonon mass-renormalization corrections are important for critical-field predictions
published_findings.numerical_prediction_metrics: not transcribed into this registry; no unsupported score is inferred from the abstract

comparison_rules.calculated_vs_measured: Keep clean-limit Eliashberg outputs separate from measured Hc/Hc1/Hc2 observations.
comparison_rules.material_state: Retain structure, Fermi-surface provenance, spectral-function version, pressure, temperature, field orientation and clean/dirty-limit assumptions.
comparison_rules.derived_quantities: Do not silently equate microscopic xi0 with near-Tc xi_GL or mix independent penetration-depth estimators.

baselines.claim_ceiling: Published first-principles / clean-limit Eliashberg critical-field database and qualitative findings; not an experimental Hc2 predictor and not independently replayed by this repository.

baselines.title: HTSC-2025: A benchmark dataset of ambient-pressure high-temperature superconductors for AI-driven critical temperature prediction

dataset.scope: Ambient-pressure, 2023-2025, predominantly conventional BCS-type theoretical predictions

baselines.split_characterization: Paper describes exclusion of test materials from training based on structural similarity and reports system-specific MAE. It is a useful structural/system-level theoretical benchmark, not a measured experimental family-OOD benchmark.
baselines.claim_ceiling: Small, theory-focused, ambient-pressure benchmark; complementary to measured-property evaluation.

baselines.title: Hierarchical inference separates superconducting feasibility from critical-temperature optimization

dataset.class_balance: described as balanced in the abstract; exact class counts not independently verified here
dataset.notes: The paper frames superconductivity as conditional inference: first estimate feasibility, then predict Tc using an expanded descriptor set. The accessible abstract reports reduced end-to-end Tc prediction error but does not expose the exact score, split manifest, dataset artifact, or checkpoint.

method.architecture: two-stage hierarchical inference with task-dependent reweighting in a shared descriptor space
method.stage_1: superconducting feasibility using an electronic-compositional backbone
method.stage_2: conditional Tc optimization with additional structural and magnetic/orbital descriptors

published_findings.reported: The two-stage framework reduces end-to-end Tc prediction error relative to a single homogeneous inference task.
published_findings.numeric_metrics: not transcribed; no unsupported numeric improvement is inferred from the abstract

baselines.split_characterization: Exact random/group/family/source/temporal split definitions and leakage controls require full-method and artifact audit before reproduction.
baselines.claim_ceiling: Published feasibility-first hierarchical ML baseline; not a verified new superconducting material and not independently reproduced by this repository.

baselines.title: Genome-inspired AI for extrapolative discovery of high-temperature superconductors
baselines.article_status: early-access accepted article; version of record may replace this version

dataset.dataset_role: reported non-superconductor control data addressing the scarcity of negative examples
dataset.notes: The abstract reports a 53,196-material DataG Non-Sc dataset. The exact row manifest, label criteria for non-superconducting status, class matching, split manifest, and downloadable dataset/checkpoint artifacts still require audit.

method.framework: AI-integrated high-throughput screening using elemental/material descriptors and existing crystallographic entries

published_candidate_predictions.example: Pu2Co17 is reported with predicted Tc approximately 89 K
published_candidate_predictions.status: unverified computational predictions; no synthesis or superconductivity confirmation is claimed here

baselines.claim_ceiling: Published extrapolative candidate-generation baseline. Candidate predictions are not observations, and radioactive actinide candidates remain computational-only absent qualified institutional review.

cross_baseline_rule: Never pool or directly rank metrics with different label authority, sample population, target definition, pressure/temperature conditions, structure inputs, or split regime.
next_reproduction_requirements: Pin exact source archive versions, licence/terms, data manifest and file hashes.
Reconstruct and verify the BEE-NET row-label versus Alexandria-ID join; assert train/validation/test disjointness.
Acquire the missing selected database and released checkpoints through permitted channels; do not infer access rights from repository visibility.
Reproduce published in-distribution metrics before running new family/prototype/source/pressure holdouts.
Report alpha2F spectral and derived Tc metrics separately from experimentally measured properties.

Qualify the August 2026 Geisler et al. clean-limit Eliashberg Hc/Hc1/Hc2 database as a separate calculated-first-principles baseline; pin its supporting information, source artifacts, method settings and exact row count before attempting replay.

Keep high-field clean-limit calculations separate from measured AutoSuperCon/NIMS values; join only on verified material state, sample form, pressure, temperature, orientation and measurement criterion.
